dedupe_keys.name: era ontology and vocabulary for european railway infrastructure and vehicles eu agency for railways

description: The ERA ontology, also published as the ERA vocabulary, is the human- and machine-readable model governed by the European Union Agency for Railways for the concepts and relationships of the European railway infrastructure, the vehicles authorised to run on it, vehicle types and evidence documents. It is a semantic representation of the application guides of the Register of Infrastructure (RINF) and of the European Register of Authorised Types of Vehicles (ERATV), built with domain experts from the RINF and ERATV working parties, and reflects Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/777 on the common specifications for the register of railway infrastructure; it also includes route book concepts. Coverage is continental (the European railway system). It is free under CC BY 4.0, published on the ERA vocabulary site and archived on Zenodo in successive versions (version 3.0.0 of the vocabulary in July 2024 and ontology version 3.3.4 in August 2026, as zipped files). Caveats: it is a model, not the data; the RINF knowledge graph holds the instances, and versions change as the regulation evolves. It lets rail digital twins, network models and compatibility checks read RINF data with consistent semantics. It is related to the Register of Infrastructure (RINF) and complements the Transmodel public transport reference model.
